I ported the program to Rust in `src/main.rs`, with `Cargo.toml` and `build.sh`. It passes all 6 cases in `node check.mjs`. I also ran it on a 55 MB file of generated words with 5 MB of random bytes, which included invalid UTF-8. The output matched the original Java program exactly, and the run took about 0.13 seconds.

Unlike the Java version, it reads all of standard input into memory at once. That's fine at the 50 MB limit. It uses only the standard library, and `cargo test` runs three small
